headline: Real Madrid draws level with Barcelona after 4-1 thrashing of Rayo Vallecano with Mbappé brace
summary: Real Madrid secured a dominant 4-1 victory over city rivals Rayo Vallecano at the Santiago Bernabéu, bouncing back from an unexpected loss eight days prior.
details: Real Madrid has drawn level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a commanding 4-1 win against Rayo Vallecano. The Spanish giants secured this position with a strong performance at home.

The victory marks a significant comeback for Real Madrid, who suffered an unexpected defeat to Real Betis just eight days earlier. They quickly established control, scoring three goals within the first 35 minutes of the match.
Kylian Mbappé opened the scoring for Real in the 14th minute from a penalty kick after Álvaro Carreras was fouled inside the box. Mbappé expertly sent Rayo's goalkeeper Emil Audero the wrong way.
Just three minutes later, Mbappé turned provider, assisting Carreras. The defender, surging down the left flank, received the ball from Mbappé and doubled Real's lead with a powerful shot.

Real Madrid's third goal came in the 35th minute from English midfielder Jude Bellingham. He capitalized on a cut-back from Vinicius Jr., orchestrating a superb attack and slotting the ball into the net with a side-foot finish.

Rayo managed to reduce the deficit early in the second half when Sergio Camello scored, hinting at a potential comeback. However, Real Madrid ultimately faced no further issues in securing their victory.
Mbappé sealed his brace in added time, firing a low and powerful shot into the far corner of the net. This goal completed his double and solidified Real Madrid's impressive win.

This triumph extends Real Madrid's formidable home record against Rayo Vallecano, having won 14 of their last 15 encounters at the Santiago Bernabéu. Barcelona is set to play against Levante, where a win would put them three points ahead of Real.

headline_marked: [[Arsenal beat Sunderland 2-0]] with Guimaraes and Saka goals, maintaining perfect start
headline: Arsenal beat Sunderland 2-0 with Guimaraes and Saka goals, maintaining perfect start
summary: Arsenal secured a hard-fought 2-0 victory over Sunderland, thanks to a crucial penalty save by David Raya and late goals from Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka. This win extends their perfect start to the season across all competitions.
details: Arsenal maintained their perfect start to the season with a challenging 2-0 victory against Sunderland. The win came after a crucial penalty save by David Raya and decisive goals from Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka.

This marks Arsenal's sixth consecutive win across all competitions, showcasing their strong form. However, the scoreline does not reflect the difficulty of the match, which proved to be one of their toughest tests this season.
The two teams clashed on Saturday, September 12, at Sunderland's home ground, the Stadium of Light. Both sides adopted a cautious approach during a tight first half, with few clear-cut chances.
The second half saw a dramatic turn of events. A penalty was awarded to Sunderland after Ezri Konsa fouled Dan Ballard in the box following a physical challenge with Brian Brobbey during a corner.
Sunderland's Enzo Le Fee stepped up for the spot-kick, but Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya made a brilliant diving save, pushing the ball wide of the post. This crucial stop kept the score level.
Just two minutes later, Arsenal capitalized on a counter-attack. Bruno Guimaraes, the former Newcastle captain, scored with a curling shot from the edge of the box, putting Arsenal ahead.

Sunderland intensified their attack in search of an equalizer, bringing on Malik Fofana. Their goalkeeper, Robin Roefs, made several excellent saves, including denying Saka, and Dan Ballard cleared a header off the line.

Arsenal's Jurrien Timber also had a goal disallowed for offside. In the closing stages, Sunderland's Reinildo received a second yellow card for impeding Saka, further increasing the pressure on the home side.
Finally, in added time, Arsenal was awarded a penalty. Bukayo Saka calmly converted the spot-kick, sealing the 2-0 victory for his team and reaffirming Arsenal's strong contention for the title.
